newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS-Sterling drop breathes life into engineers.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Sterling drop breathes life into engineers.

text.p: Shares in Britain's leading engineering companies, battered for months by the sharp appreciation of sterling, rebounded on Tuesday as the currency stumbled for a second session, dealers and analysts said.

Engineers and other firms with major overseas earnings have underperformed for months as analysts cut earnings forecasts, reflecting the surging pound, which has priced exports out of overseas markets and squeezed the value of their foreign currency earnings.
Yet hopes that the pound may have peaked sent companies such as TI Group Plc and GKN Plc up by more than five percent in the FTSE 100 index while other overseas earners also rose sharply.
Smiths Industries Plc shares added 24-1/2p to 780, Siebe Plc advanced 26p to 10.69-1/2 pounds, British Steel Plc rose 2-3/4p to 161-1/2 and Burmah Castrol Plc rose 21-1/2p to 10.59 pounds.
Analysts cautioned however that sterling remained at relatively high levels and said more profit downgrades could be forthcoming if British currency's retreat proved to be short-lived.

After surging 17 percent since the beginning of the year to a peak of 3.0878 marks on July 23, the pound tumbled seven pfennigs during the last two days and was holding at around 2.9950 marks at midday on Tuesday.
"(Sterling) is still near 3.0 marks and if it stays at these levels, there could be more downgrades," said SocGen engineering analyst Andy Chambers.

Powered by expectations of higher British interest rates, the pound's advance has imposed a squeeze on manufacturing industry, prompting warnings from some that the economy could lapse into recession during 1998.

The Confederation of British Industry for instance warned on Monday that new export orders for medium and small sized firms fell at their fastest rate for six years in the past four months. "The seemingly inexorable rise in sterling is...placing a tight squeeze on exporters' margins," said Tony Bonner, a CBI spokesman.

According to data from Reuters Securities 3000, the UK engineering sector has underperformed the FTSE 100 share index by some 22 percent so far this year as the strength of sterling cut into profits of those with heavy overseas exposure.
Tim Bennett, an analyst with Morgan Stanley, called the rally a knee-jerk reaction the profit-taking on the foreign exchange market and said it could be short-lived.
"There was some real panic when sterling rose above 3.0 marks, so this is just a sigh of relief," Bennett said.
"But we'd need to see sterling fall below 2.95 before we'll start looking at our profit forecasts. At the moment, we're still on the wrong side of 2.95," Bennett said.
SocGen's Chambers said he wouldn't revisit his earnings estimates unless sterling fell below 2.70 marks.
Some analysts and dealers reckoned sterling may have topped out amid perceptions that interest rates, which have been raised three times in the last three months, will remain steady in the near-term.

"Investors are looking beyond this year...in terms of company profitability, the long period of sterling's strength and aggressive interest rate moves," a dealer added. "They are wondering whether we should be at these levels."
